To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the first chalcogenide amplifier and that we have demonstrated internal gain in a chalcogenide thin film planar optical waveguide amplifier.
the first Er-doped As 2 S 3 thin-film waveguide amplifier has been demonstrated, with a gain of 1.4 dB at 1.53 µm, a saturation power of 0.8 mW, and a net gain bandwidth of 20 nm.
the first chalcogenide waveguides have been fabricated and the first chalcogenic waveguides have shown gain in the telecommunications wavelength range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of optical fiber amplifier based on a chalcogenide host.
the fabrication and characterization of chalcogenide glasses and glassy thin films.
the development of new chalcogenide glasses with high nonlinear refractive index and high optical damage threshold.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chalcogenide materials have the potential to provide a new class of low-loss optical fiber amplifiers for telecommunications and other applications, but that the development of suitable materials and device structures is still at an early stage.
Er-doped chalcogenide glasses are a promising candidate for low-loss and low-cost planar waveguiding amplifiers in the telecommunications band. Proc. SPIE 6132, Photonics North 2005:
the results obtained in this work show the potential of chalcogenide glasses as gain media for optical amplifiers and lasers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the first gain measurements in chalcogenide waveguides.
we have demonstrated for the first-time, internal gain in a chalcogenide waveguide.
the gain in chalcogenide waveguides is not as high as in silicates, but is sufficient to demonstrate gain in the telecommunications window.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chalcogenide gain medium is not limited to bulk form, but can also be used as a gain medium for integrated optics.
the internal gain is a function of pump power and is observed at a wavelength of 1,550 nm, which is a wavelength that is used in telecommunications.
chalcogenide glasses are an attractive platform for the development of low-loss, high-gain, and compact integrated amplifiers for mid-infrared and telecommunications applications.
